advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconsider whether an _ignore_lock_artifacts failure should abort commit-and-push entirely, or degrade to a warning while still attempting locked commit/push.
evidence: src/rebar/_store/push.py:546: `detail = "could not exclude tracker lock artifacts from staging"`
src/rebar/_store/push.py:503: `if resolved.returncode != 0 or not resolved.stdout.strip():` -> `return False`
advisory.finding: _ignore_lock_artifacts conflates an ancillary hygiene step (excluding lock artifacts) with a hard delivery gate: if `git rev-parse --git-path` fails, returns empty, or the exclude file raises OSError (e.g. permission/read error), it returns False and the entire commit-and-push is aborted and classified as 'stage-failed', even when the tracker tree is otherwise perfectly committable and deliverable.
scenarios: An info/exclude that is read-only or on a filesystem returning OSError blocks all commit-and-push delivery for that tracker rather than degrading the exclusion step alone.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the unsynchronized info/exclude append (outside the write lock) is acceptable, or move exclusion inside the lock.
advisory.finding: The info/exclude append in _ignore_lock_artifacts is performed BEFORE the write lock is acquired, so two concurrent commit_and_push_tickets_branch callers can interleave the read-modify-append of .git/info/exclude; dedup is by whole-line splitlines so the worst case is duplicate exclude lines rather than corruption, but the mutation of a shared .git file is unsynchronized relative to the store's write lock.
scenarios: Two rebar processes committing the same shared tracker concurrently could both read a missing pattern and both append it.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that a tracker containing `.ticket-write.lock`/`.ticket-write.lock.d/` is committed WITHOUT those artifacts (exclude applied), plus a test forcing the exclude-write to fail so the `stage-failed` strict error / default warning-return path is exercised.
evidence: push.py:500-523 defines `_ignore_lock_artifacts` which appends lock patterns to info/exclude and returns False on OSError
push.py:545-549: `if not _ignore_lock_artifacts(canonical): ... _raise_if_strict(strict, "stage-failed", detail, ...)` — this branch is never triggered by any test
search of tests for `_ignore_lock_artifacts` and `ticket-write.lock` returns no test that exercises the exclude-write or the False path against commit_and_push_tickets_branch

ABSENCE: no test creates a tracker containing a `.ticket-write.lock` artifact and asserts it is absent from the committed tree, so a regression that commits the lock files (the whole purpose of the helper) would go undetected
advisory.finding: The new `_ignore_lock_artifacts` helper and the `stage-failed`/'could not exclude tracker lock artifacts' branch it gates are untested: no test verifies that `.ticket-write.lock`/`.ticket-write.lock.d/` are written to info/exclude (or that a lock artifact present in the tree stays out of the resulting commit), nor that the False return path yields a `stage-failed` PushDeliveryError (strict) / warning+early-return (default).
scenarios: An implicit-legacy store commits its own lock files onto the tickets branch
info/exclude is unwritable and the helper returns False, and a strict caller must receive stage-failed
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a unit test that seeds a `.ticket-write.lock` file in the tracker before calling commit_and_push_tickets_branch and asserts `git show HEAD:.ticket-write.lock` returns non-zero; and a test that monkeypatches open/rev-parse (or makes info/exclude unwritable) so `_ignore_lock_artifacts` returns False and asserts a `stage-failed` PushDeliveryError under strict and a clean early-return + warning under default.
